key_insight: LizTail shows that a systolic array can be made both shape-adaptive and parallelism-aware by reconfiguring computation in predefined segments instead of at individual PEs.
engineering_relevance: This matters for CNNs and LLM decoding because it improves utilization on skinny matrices, small-batch workloads, and multi-partition operators without the full overhead of fully flexible interconnects.
method: Partitions a 128×128 array into 32 fixed 128×4 segments.
Adds only endpoint connectivity, including trimming, 180° turn-back extension, and distributed execution across segments.
Uses differentiated PE datapaths plus segment-aware CEB/SIB buffers, guided by a hardware-constrained mapper.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports geometric-mean speedups of 5.02× on CNN inference and 25.67× on LLM decoding over a TPU-like array, with EDP reduced by up to 38.23×.
watch_item: The design depends on constrained segment-level reconfiguration, so performance may be limited by mapper quality and by the overheads of implementing segment-aware buffers and endpoint connections in hardware.
paper_title: LizTail: Unifying Shape Adaptation and Spatial Parallelism with Segment-Reconfigurable Systolic Arrays
